strengths: UNREAL addresses an important problem: unreliable minority-class pseudo-labels under severe label imbalance. Retrieving existing unlabeled nodes avoids synthesizing node features and graph connections, and the proposed selection pipeline is intuitively motivated.

The empirical coverage is substantial: five datasets, three GNN architectures, imbalance ratios up to 100, and five repetitions. Reported gains are often meaningful; at ratio 10, GCN F1 improves over the strongest compared baseline by 4.30 points on Cora and 8.62 points on CiteSeer.

The appendix includes pseudo-label accuracy diagnostics, component ablations, sensitivity studies, and extensive experimental settings. These provide useful evidence beyond aggregate benchmark scores and support partial reproducibility. No specific material ethical concern is evident from the benchmark-based study.
weaknesses: Internal inconsistencies undermine confidence in the diagnostic evidence. In Table 8, GCN at ratio 5 reports 11,593.6 aligned and 2,308.4 discarded nodes, totaling 13,902 despite only 13,632 unlabeled nodes. Table 9 reports 94.20 ± 8.04 for GraphSAGE at ratio 50 as a mean and standard error over five runs; for five accuracy values bounded by 100 with that mean, the maximum empirical standard error is 5.8. These may be reporting errors, but corrected tables and run-level results are needed.

Novelty relative to the closest prior method is insufficiently established. The cited M3S already uses clustering agreement to filter pseudo-labels, closely overlapping DPAM, yet it is not directly benchmarked. The DPAM-plus-confidence ablation helps, but a comparison with M3S adapted to class imbalance under matching selection and training budgets is important for attributing the gains. A fixed-weight rank-aggregation baseline would also clarify the specific value of RBO weighting.

Some algorithmic definitions are consequentially ambiguous. Equation 7 combines ordered node lists without explicitly defining the per-node numerical ranks being combined. Equation 5 measures distance to the assigned class center, whereas Section 4.3 treats it as distance to the nearest class center; assignment through a cluster center does not guarantee this equivalence. Algorithm 1 also omits explicit implementation of the per-class selection quota and updating the unlabeled pool.

The practical efficiency argument is incomplete. Appendices D.3–D.4 specify 40–100 training rounds, with up to 2,000 epochs per subsequent round, plus repeated clustering. No runtime or peak-memory measurements establish the overall computational tradeoff. Baseline out-of-memory results on one GPU demonstrate implementation-specific feasibility differences, rather than a comprehensive scalability advantage.

The superiority claims need qualification. On Computers-Random, GraphSAGE UNREAL trails GraphENS+TAM by 3.17 balanced-accuracy points and 1.73 F1 points; Flickr GAT also loses on balanced accuracy. Furthermore, changing the imbalance ratio beyond 20 changes the training split and increases majority-class supervision, so those comparisons do not isolate imbalance alone. The promising reported gains do not outweigh the unresolved evidence and comparison gaps.
